phase-plan.purpose: Replace raw content-pack bundle object access with schema-generated typed codecs, serializer helpers, and language-targeted code assets so authored content can be marshalled consistently into runtime consumers.
phase-plan.scope: Runtime load-path analysis, quicktype-driven codegen design, and implementation of generated loaders/code assets for TypeScript first, with matching JSON-schema-driven outputs for C++/Unreal consumption. Unreal `.uasset` generation remains an editor/import step, not a Node-side binary writer. No new content-editor UI in this slice.

file.description: Current runtime fetch/parse boundary that reads raw bundle JSON and selected pack objects directly.
Current coercion boundary that casts raw bundle data into vector overrides instead of decoding a typed pack.
Existing codegen already emits manifest/schema/stub outputs; replace or complement this with quicktype-generated marshal/serializer/code-asset outputs.
Zod-backed pack schemas already exist here and can anchor generated codecs/loaders.
Authored schema/content root that generated codecs must target.

task.description: Document the current bundle load path and identify every raw-object access point that bypasses typed decoding.
Design the quicktype-generated TypeScript codec/serializer surface for authored packs and define parity outputs for C++/Unreal code assets.
Implement the TypeScript decode/load path and replace Kaplay runtime raw bundle access with typed pack loaders.

questions.question: Generated language outputs must go beyond model stubs and include marshal/serializer-oriented code assets.

decision.summary: Runtime consumers should treat the content pack bundle as transport and decode typed pack objects immediately after parsing, with generated code coming from JSON Schema via quicktype rather than handwritten Zod-only contracts.
decision.impact: Keeps authored schema as the source of truth, makes future Unreal/runtime integration deterministic, and avoids hand-maintained contract duplication.
